description: React components for transactional emails, email templates, landing pages, invoices, reports and PDFs. Render email-safe HTML, responsive web HTML and print-ready PDF HTML from one component tree.
rules: Install @unlayer/react-elements. A template has one root: <Email>, <Page>, <Document> (print/PDF) or <Canvas> (an image).

A root, a Section and a Column stack their children; a Row puts its Columns side by side and stacks them on phones. Text goes in Heading, Paragraph or Text, with Span, Link, LineBreak and MergeTag inside them; no raw HTML outside an Html block.
Styles go in style={{ ... }}, never as props, and a number is px. There are no margins: space between blocks is their parent's gap, space inside a box its padding.

await render(element) returns { html, text, diagnostics } for the output its root says, and rejects with an ElementsError listing the template's problems; validate(element) checks a template without rendering it. toDesign() from @unlayer/react-elements/builder returns Unlayer design JSON that the Unlayer editor opens with loadDesign(), and fromDesign() reads one back as a template.
Start with packages/react/docs/README.md for task selection. Runnable transactional email, provider, PDF, and visual editing recipes are in packages/react/docs/ and examples/content-workflows/.
Elements renders HTML, not email delivery or PDF bytes. Send email HTML through a provider; print Document HTML with Playwright Chromium for a real PDF.
For shared templates, pass render() a root, or a component that returns one. Your own components and Fragments inside it can return any of the components.

render() renders the template once with React (hooks, Context and your own components work). A component that is async or suspends is an error: load data first. Every component and prop: packages/react/PRIMITIVES.md.

To move React Email templates to Elements, run `npx @unlayer/migrate <folder> --report migration.md`, read the report, then add `--write`. It keeps props, loops and conditions, checks every template against the original, and lists what differs. After converting a template by hand, check it with `npx @unlayer/migrate compare <original> <migrated>`. See packages/react/docs/migrate-from-react-email.md.
To open React Email templates in the Unlayer editor, run `npx @unlayer/migrate <folder> --out <dir> --design` and pass each `<name>.design.json` to `loadDesign()`. See examples/react-email-in-editor.

To preview Elements code without installing, open https://examples.unlayer.com/examples/elements-playground/#code=<base64url of the code> (plain JSX, no imports; add &mode=email|page|document). In WebMCP browsers the page exposes a render_elements tool that returns the HTML.
